bib.title: Planning with Large Language Models for Code Generation

question: Can a planning algorithm be integrated with a pre-trained code-generation Transformer to generate better programs than conventional beam search and the sampling + filtering scheme?
hypothesis: Using the pass rate on public test cases as a lookahead reward during decoding yields better programs, more sample-efficiently, than using test cases only to filter finished programs.
contributions: PG-TD: Monte-Carlo-tree-search-style lookahead guiding Transformer decoding; model-agnostic, no grammar knowledge needed
Caching mechanisms (tree structure caching, sequence caching) that share information between Transformer beam search and tree search
Evaluation on APPS and CodeContests showing higher pass rate than baselines, and controllable generation (concise, commented code) by changing the reward

method.summary: PG-TD runs an MCTS over tokens. Selection uses P-UCB weighted by the Transformer's next-token probability, expansion adds the top-k tokens, evaluation completes the program with Transformer beam search and scores it by pass rate on public test cases, and the max reward is backpropagated. No weights change at decode time; PG-TD outputs can optionally be used to fine-tune the model.

inference.decoding: PG-TD: P-UCB tree search; top-k expansion; evaluation step by Transformer beam search. Baselines: beam search (beam 5), sampling+filtering (top-3 sampling), SMCG-TD
inference.samples: Budget = number of Transformer generations: 256 (Table 1), 512 (Table 5); 512 programs max for S+F, population 200 for SMCG-TD. Single run, no seeds reported.
inference.prompting: Codex: problem description in a block comment, 'Python 3' header. Test-case generation: HumanEval prompt ending with assert statement (following Chen et al. 2022).

parameters.c (P-UCB exploration): 2, 4, 6; c=4 best; main tables use c=4
parameters.reward: pass rate on public test cases; reward of partial program 0
parameters.caching: tree structure caching and sequence caching

limits: Relies on test cases; authors say auto-generated tests partly address this (Sec 5, App B)
More computationally expensive than plain beam search (runs beam search many times) (Sec 5)
Advantage over S+F shrinks at larger budgets (512 generations) and S+F matches/beats on some strict accuracy and pass@100 (App A)
Backbones are APPS-finetuned GPT-2/GPT-Neo (2022); Codex tested on 100-problem subset only; Codex is deprecated
No seeds, variance or significance tests reported
Public/private split of APPS is the authors' even split of test cases, not official
Sequence caching with b>1 may underestimate values (App D.2)
Evaluation step sampling done once per node (App A)

terms.definition: Planning-Guided Transformer Decoding: tree search over tokens that uses Transformer beam search to evaluate nodes and public-test pass rate as reward
sample many complete programs, run public tests, return the one with highest pass rate
the percentage of the problems where the generated programs pass all the private test cases
